title: Invariant and Invalid State
definition: An invariant is a condition that must remain true for a model to be valid; an invalid state violates at least one required condition.
purpose: Make business truth explicit and prevent or reject contradictory data before it spreads.
history: Invariants connect mathematical reasoning, abstract data types, design by contract, databases, and domain modeling.
mental_model: A guardrail around the set of states the program is willing to represent as valid.
analogy: A ticket whose end time cannot precede its start time; useful because validity depends on relationships, not only individual field types.
common_mistakes: Validating after invalid data is shared
Using defaults that hide missing facts
industry_notes: Make invalid states harder to create with narrow constructors, explicit variants, and validation at untrusted boundaries.
ai_notes: Challenge AI models with invalid combinations and ask which layer preserves each invariant.
interview_notes: Ask for a cross-field invariant and a design that prevents its violation.
